hero.title: File:St. Valentine's Day Massacre (52338016185).jpg
hero.artist: Stephen Hogan from Chicago, United States
hero.description:
The St. Valentine's Day Massacre happened here on Feb. 14, 1929. This is where the S.M.C. Cartage Company warehouse formerly stood until it was demolished in 1967.
Al Capone's men, disguised as police, shot seven members of George "Bugs" Moran's gang (actually five plus two non-gangsters, a retired optometrist and a car mechanic.)
This is a rare look at the site without the fence blocking it. The fence was knocked down and removed after a recent lightning strike.

Located at 2122 N. Clark St.

gallery.filename: National Museum of Crime and Punishmen - Saint Valentine's Day Massacre brick (2868502113).jpg
gallery.title: File:National Museum of Crime and Punishmen - Saint Valentine's Day Massacre brick (2868502113).jpg
gallery.source: National Museum of Crime and Punishmen - Saint Valentine's Day Massacre brick (2868502113)
gallery.description:
Saint Valentine's Day Massacre brick displayed at the National Museum of Crime & Punishment, Washington, D.C.


“


The St. Valentine's Day Massacre
This bullet-impacted brick was the first to be removed from the Massacre site prior to its demolition. Note the circular markings, made by the Chicago Police Department ballistics detectives in their investigations to determine how many gunmen were likely to have participated in the Massacre, and what weapons were used.
The St. Valentine's Day Massacre was the name given to the Winter 1929 machine-gun slaying of seven men in a Prohibition-Era conflict between the two most powerful Chicago gangs: the South Side Italian squad led by Al "Scarface" Capone and the North Side Irish/German gang led by George "Bugs" Moran.
Courtesy of the Arthur Nash Collection


”
categories: National Museum of Crime and Punishment

gallery.title: File:Site of St. Valentine's Day Massacre (3710289226).jpg
gallery.artist: Stephen Hogan from Chicago, United States
gallery.description:
The St. Valentine's Day Massacre happened here on Feb. 14, 1929. This is where the S.M.C. Cartage Company warehouse stood until it was demolished in 1967.
Al Capone's men, disguised as police, shot seven members of George "Bugs" Moran's gang (actually five plus two non-gangsters, a retired optometrist and a car mechanic.) The actual shooting happened at the far left side of this photo, a few feet away from the alley where this was taken.

gallery.filename: St. Valentine's Day Massacre (3707741689).jpg
gallery.title: File:St. Valentine's Day Massacre (3707741689).jpg
gallery.artist: Stephen Hogan from Chicago, United States
gallery.description:
This is the sidewalk leading the location of the St. Valentine's Day Massacre. Al Capone's men dressed like police in a stolen Cadillac made to look like a police car pulled alongside the curb just north of here. They entered George "Bugs" Moran's S.M.C. Cartage Co. warehouse, forced seven men there to stand against a wall and murdered them with machine guns and other firearms. Five of them were members of Moran's gang, two were non-gangsters. Moran was expected to be among them but was not.
Across the street you can see a red building with a black awning that Capone's men used as a lookout directly across from the warehouse.

Picture taken at 2106 N Clark St. looking north.

gallery.artist: Stephen Hogan from Chicago, United States
gallery.description:
The St. Valentine's Day Massacre happened here on Feb. 14, 1929. This is where the S.M.C. Cartage Company warehouse stood until it was demolished in 1967.  
Al Capone's men, disguised as police, shot seven members of George "Bugs" Moran's gang (actually five gangsters plus two non-gangsters, a retired optometrist and a car mechanic.)
The building on the left with the marble columns was there at the time and can be seen in period news photos of the massacre.  The empty lot to the right is where the warehouse stood before its demolition.

Located at 2122 N. Clark St.
